docs.title: DisasterWorld
docs.text:
DisasterWorld evaluates survivor-search systems in damaged simulated environments. This repository provides a local runtime, mission configuration, survivor-only task generation and saved-report evaluation. Isaac Sim loads downloaded scenes; AirStack supplies the provided aerial autonomy stack.

Start with installation, then configure and run an episode. You can use the provided policies or add your own ROS baseline.

docs.title: Run an episode
docs.text:
After setup and installing the scenes, start a four-robot Frontier mission:

./dw run --robots 4 --baseline frontier --accept-isaac-license

run validates configuration, prepares search areas and robot settings, starts the simulator and policies, and saves episode artifacts for evaluation.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Use the navigation sidebar for dataset structure, survivor generation, baseline integration and troubleshooting. Mission configuration describes fleet sizes, partitioned or shared bounds, and local or URL-based inference.

Maintainer TODO — before release

Publish the dataset bundle and fill in its download URL and checksum. Include local USD assets, scene manifests, survivor annotations and verified spawns in the bundle format. Complete end-to-end simulation validation and the paper reproduction audit before release.

For detailed RayFronts documentation, see the original RayFronts repository. For AirStack setup and interfaces, see the AirStack documentation.

docs.title: Configure and run
docs.text:
Edit configs/default.yaml or create an override YAML. Paths are relative to the configuration file, not the shell's current directory. Unknown keys are errors.

scene: fire/suburban/level_1
survivor_variant: 1
robots: 4
baseline: frontier
mission_seconds: 600
search:
  region: affected_area
  assignment: partitioned
inference:
  yolo_url: null
  blip_url: null
  vlm_url: null
  gpu: 0
simulation:
  gpu: 0

scene selects disaster/locality/damage level; survivor_variant selects a published survivor layout. robots uses the first N verified spawn points from the scene manifest. Missions share a start time and a simulated-time budget after takeoff. Policy startup and mapper initialization currently count within the mission budget; HTTP inference services are warmed beforehand. Fixed navigation limits are configured in MIGHTY; the runtime uses the upstream navigation interface.

docs.title: Search areas
docs.text:
region: affected_area uses the bundle's disaster boundary; whole_map uses the map boundary. custom uses custom_polygon. These polygons must be convex and given in world XY meters. assignment: partitioned splits the polygon into deterministic equal-area strips. shared gives every robot the entire polygon. The generated assignments.svg previews the allocation.

./dw run --robots 4 --baseline frontier --accept-isaac-license
./dw run --robots 4 --baseline conavgpt --accept-isaac-license

The CoNavGPT command selects whole_map and shared automatically. It starts one team planner on a bridged DDS domain, rather than a separate cooperative planner per robot. Frontier, Lawnmower and VLFM use per-robot policies. RAVEN uses its RayFronts adapter; consult RayFronts' own docs for mapper usage.

docs.title: Inference
docs.text:
Leave the URLs as null, none or blank for local inference. DisasterWorld starts the services required by the selected baseline on inference.gpu; you do not need to supply server addresses for this mode.

To use an already-running server, supply its base address. The example host gpu-machine represents your server; these are not hosted endpoints provided by DisasterWorld.

Setting Example base address Expected API Required by yolo_url http://gpu-machine:8200 GET /health, POST /detect; our YOLO/SAM image, box and mask formats Lawnmower, Frontier, VLFM, CoNavGPT blip_url http://gpu-machine:8100 GET /health, POST /score; our BLIP image/text scoring format VLFM vlm_url http://gpu-machine:8000/v1 GET /models, POST /chat/completions; OpenAI-compatible vision messages CoNavGPT

The included servers are supplied by asm_offboard. YOLO and BLIP use its custom HTTP protocols; another implementation must preserve the same request and response formats. The VLM server must accept image messages and serve the configured model, currently Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct.

Setting a URL suppresses that local service. URLs are reached from inside the robot containers: use a reachable hostname/IP for a host service. localhost inside a container refers to that container. VLM credentials come from the environment variable named by vlm_api_key_env, default DW_VLM_API_KEY; they are not written into run configuration. YOLO and BLIP currently use no API-key authentication.

Maintainer TODO — remote deployment

Add provider deployment recipes and authenticated YOLO/BLIP clients. Existing base-address configuration does not provision a cloud server. See the remote inference plan.

docs.title: Artifacts and shutdown
docs.text:
run validates configuration and generates all mission files before starting containers. For optional inspection, ./dw config check validates settings without running a mission, and ./dw prepare --robots 4 --baseline frontier --output .local/preview writes mission files and an assignment preview. Neither command is required before run.

./dw run --dry-run resolves the launch without starting containers. A completed run saves configuration, version pins, per-robot reports/trajectories, policy logs and container logs under results_root. Policies receive public bounds and observations; survivor ground truth is kept for the host evaluator. ./dw down stops the current DisasterWorld project. Use distinct runtime.project and network_subnet values for simultaneous installations.

Maintainer TODO — simulator validation

Complete a frozen-scene end-to-end acceptance run. Verify sensor alignment, common timing, report frames and policy settings against the paper before release.

docs.title: Add a baseline
docs.text:
The baseline template is a small ROS 2 AirStack module. Copy it, rename the module/package, and register it using airstack.sh module add PATH --no-hooks. The template's node consumes odometry and public task bounds; it publishes a nonempty path to MIGHTY. It has no survivor labels or ground-truth access.

Implement observation-driven goal selection in example.py, subscribe to the required camera/depth/LiDAR topics and publish disasterworld_msgs/DetectionReport only when your perception system produces a survivor location. Reports must identify their coordinate frame (map or world), observation timestamp and stable report ID. Local map coordinates are translated using that robot's spawn; a team policy can publish world coordinates directly.

For timed benchmark execution, register your policy in config.BASELINES, add a launch command in dw_runtime/task_server.py, and declare which local inference services it needs in inference_plan. This explicit adapter step is required in the initial release; there is not yet a dynamic policy registry. Keep the existing common start/deadline and evaluator report recording.

A separate stack can drive a different robot through its own controller, using the downloaded USD scenes and the same public bounds/report format. The provided one-line setup supports the aerial AirStack/MIGHTY path; arbitrary robots require their own simulation/controller adapter.

Declare dependencies in the module manifest or its container layer. See the AirStack module documentation for module packaging. The template publishes no synthetic detections; replace its example waypoint policy before evaluating it as a search baseline.

docs.title: Dataset bundles
docs.text:
The runtime loads local frozen USD scenes and requires no lab Nucleus access. Archives must contain scenes/ at their root and regular files/directories only; external archive links and path traversal are rejected.

Maintainer TODO — publish the bundle

Fill in the public archive URL and SHA-256 in the default configuration after validating and publishing the bundle.

Each scene has a manifest at scenes/DISASTER/LOCALITY/level_N/manifest.json:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "units": "meters",
  "world_frame": "world",
  "whole_map": [[-100,-100],[100,-100],[100,100],[-100,100]],
  "affected_area": [[-80,-60],[80,-60],[80,60],[-80,60]],
  "spawn_points": [[0,0,1],[3,0,1],[6,0,1],[9,0,1]],
  "variants": {
    "1": {"stage_file": "variants/1/scene.usda", "ground_truth_file": "variants/1/ground_truth.json"}
  },
  "geometry_file": "geometry/scene.usda",
  "placement_candidates_file": "placement_candidates.json"
}

The example describes the format, not a published benchmark task. Provide entries for all available published variants. Spawn points must be verified free-space positions for the chosen aircraft; the runtime checks numeric validity, map containment and separation, but does not certify collision safety.

USD layers must use meters, Z-up, a /World root and portable local references. Include every referenced asset, texture and dependency. Do not ship omniverse:// references into the lab server. The publisher validates USD dependencies and physical properties in Isaac Sim before release. Downloads verify the archive checksum, and each run checks its selected scene manifest and required paths automatically.

Ground truth contains world_frame: "world" and a survivors array of objects with unique id and [x,y,z] position. Ground truth is supplied to the evaluator, never mounted into policy containers. See evaluation for optional reference route metadata.

geometry_file must be people-free damaged geometry. It and placement_candidates_file are required only for survivor-only generation.

Maintainer TODO — placement assets

Prepare the people-free geometry, posed survivor assets and verified placement candidates from the research dataset before publishing the bundle.

docs.title: Evaluate saved episodes
docs.text:
./dw evaluate --run results/RUN_DIRECTORY --matching-radius YOUR_RADIUS_METERS

The evaluator requires a completed episode from every robot, evaluator ground truth in world coordinates and a positive matching radius chosen for the experiment. Scoring uses the simulated time a report reaches the task server, relative to the common mission start, so processing/communication delay remains part of the search system. The publisher's header stamp is retained separately. Reports outside the budget receive no credit. Each report matches its nearest survivor within the radius; duplicate reports do not add discoveries.

TIP integrates normalized survivor progress over the mission: for N survivors, budget T, and first report times t_i, TIP = sum(1 - t_i/T) / N. Progress is the fraction discovered by the deadline. Saved trajectories provide the team path length.

PPL requires a validated collision-free minimum reference route for the exact discovered survivor subset, robot count and starts. The evaluator leaves PPL unavailable when that route is absent, rather than substituting straight-line distances through debris. Reference generation/validation is a dataset release gate. A no-discovery run has PPL zero.

Optional reference_routes entries in ground truth use survivor_ids, distance_m, validated_collision_free: true, robot_count, and start_positions. Starts must match the recorded mission-start positions after takeoff, rather than ground spawn locations. The publisher is responsible for the route's minimum-path validity. Failed/incomplete episodes are refused. Output is written to metrics.json; synthetic generated tasks are identified in run metadata.

This is an initial report-based evaluator. Paper-equivalent experiments still require auditing the matching rule/radius, reference routes, survivor definition, camera geometry, policy parameters and timing against the manuscript. Default CLI values are not a reproduction guarantee.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The provided containers support Linux x86_64, NVIDIA GPUs and ROS 2 Jazzy. Install Git, Python 3.10+ with venv, Docker Engine, Docker Compose 2.30+ and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Verify nvidia-smi and Docker GPU access before setup. Isaac Sim's requirements determine the simulator's supported hardware and driver.

git clone https://github.com/DisasterWorld/DisasterWorld.git disasterworld && cd disasterworld && ./dw setup

Setup creates a small Python virtual environment, obtains pinned AirStack/MIGHTY/module checkouts in .runtime, registers modules using the AirStack CLI, builds isolated container images and builds the ROS overlay. Optional CMU credentials are prompted interactively, with Skip as the default. ./dw setup --public-only skips those prompts. Credentials and caches stay in ignored local directories. Setup never resets tracked changes in an existing checkout.

Maintainer TODO — public repository access

Make the release repositories public when ready. During private preparation, setup requires GitHub access to the repositories even when AirLab credentials are skipped.

The first build and model downloads need internet and substantial disk space; exact resource requirements depend on the selected policies and scenes. Inference and simulation may share GPU 0. Two GPUs are not a requirement, but a single GPU must fit the simulator and selected models. Smaller fleets and Frontier/Lawnmower are useful starting points.

Maintainer TODO — dataset download

Set the archive URL and SHA-256 in the default configuration when the bundle is published.

Download the scenes with:

./dw dataset download

Alternatively unpack the released self-contained bundle into dataset.root. Existing nonempty dataset directories are not replaced. Setup supports --skip-build followed by ./dw build for inspecting registration before an expensive build.

Then run a mission; configuration validation and task preparation happen automatically:

./dw run --robots 4 --baseline frontier --accept-isaac-license

Running Isaac Sim requires acceptance of NVIDIA's EULA and privacy policy. --accept-isaac-license sets ACCEPT_EULA=Y and OMNI_ENV_PRIVACY_CONSENT=Y for the simulator container. Setup does not accept these terms for you.

To work on the three repositories together, use ./dw setup --module-dir .. --public-only. This uses sibling module folders instead of downloading release revisions. The release lock records the supported AirStack and Pegasus pins; other AirStack versions are not assumed compatible.

docs.title: DisasterWorld integration
docs.text:
The release lock pins a tested integration target, rather than assuming every AirStack version is interchangeable. Setup clones upstream AirStack, registers local module paths in modules.repos, and invokes its module CLI. Generated overlays mount ROS packages and simulator launch scripts without modifying upstream task messages.

Component DisasterWorld responsibility asm_disasterworld_sim Load a downloaded frozen USD scene and configured aircraft spawns asm_disasterworld_ros Search policies, the SurvivorSearch action, reports, mission coordination asm_mighty Pinned upstream motion planner; fixed speed configured in YAML asm_offboard Shared local detector, BLIP and VLM services, compatible URL contracts asm_rayfronts RayFronts container and camera-pose connection used by RAVEN

The simulator uses upstream Pegasus. Research camera render gates, tick skipping and time slicing are excluded. SurvivorSearch is a benchmark-owned action; NavigateTask and SemanticSearchTask are not extended. Policies publish nonempty /robot_N/global_plan paths to the upstream MIGHTY follower after takeoff.

The runtime gives each aircraft a ROS domain and bridges named observation/plan topics for cooperative policies. All containers use the benchmark's isolated Compose project/network. Private survivor annotations are available only to simulation/evaluation.

For detailed RayFronts documentation, see the original RayFronts repository. AirStack module conventions are documented in the AirStack documentation. These integrations can move into upstream AirStack independently of DisasterWorld. Compatibility with later revisions requires explicit adapter testing and updating the lock.

docs.title: Remote inference plan
docs.text:
Maintainer planning document

Implement and validate remote deployment recipes before adding them to the user setup instructions. This page records planned work; local inference is the provided setup today.

The initial release starts required model services locally. Configuration already accepts existing compatible YOLO, BLIP and VLM URLs; it does not create cloud resources or offer managed endpoints. Empty URLs select local services.

docs.title: Existing contracts
docs.text:
YOLO uses the detector's image-plus-prompt JSON API, with boxes and encoded masks consumed by the search adapter. BLIP accepts encoded images and text and returns image-text matching scores. The VLM uses OpenAI-compatible /v1/models and /v1/chat/completions with vision messages. The code in asm_offboard is the authoritative contract.

A remote service must preserve model revision, thresholds, preprocessing, mask serialization and score interpretation. Compatible VLM providers must support the configured model's vision behavior; an arbitrary chat endpoint is insufficient. Keep RayFronts' CUDA IPC encoder transport local until a separate network protocol is implemented.

docs.title: Planned deployment work
docs.text:
1. Add authenticated HTTPS clients for YOLO/BLIP and consistent timeouts, retry limits and health/version reporting. VLM keys already come from environment variables.
  2. Package model-specific deployment recipes using the same locked weights and API schemas. RunPod, Modal or self-managed university/cloud GPU hosts are candidates to assess; none is currently supported. OSMO can be an optional deployment path for institutions with access, not a prerequisite.
  3. Measure latency and bandwidth for fleets, avoid uploading unnecessary frames, and handle endpoint loss explicitly. Do not silently substitute a different model after a failure.
  4. Record model/server revisions, round-trip latency and deployment mode in run artifacts. Keep cloud cost/credentials outside benchmark configuration and report remote-inference experiments separately when latency changes mission behavior.
  5. Test TLS/authentication, schema compatibility, concurrent fleets and disconnects before publishing provider recipes.

docs.title: Generate additional search tasks
docs.text:
Select the original disaster layout with --scene, such as fire/urban/level_1. The generator loads that scene's people-free damaged geometry and its own verified placement candidates. It samples survivor positions and poses on that layout while keeping buildings, debris and other damaged geometry fixed.

./dw survivors generate --scene fire/urban/level_1 \
  --seed 7 --count 20 --output data/disasterworld/generated/fire-urban-l1-task-7

Then run the generated task on the same scene:

./dw run --scene fire/urban/level_1 \
  --generated-task generated/fire-urban-l1-task-7/generated_task.json \
  --robots 4 --baseline frontier --accept-isaac-license

--scene selects scenes/fire/urban/level_1/manifest.json in this example. Its geometry_file and placement_candidates_file identify the original geometry and the candidates validated for that exact layout. The generator checks the geometry checksum before sampling, and the task records its source scene and geometry checksum. A run rejects a task if its scene or geometry differs.

Generated tasks live inside dataset.root so USD references work in the simulator container. generated_task is a dataset-relative manifest path. Published variants remain separate; generated tasks are marked synthetic in evaluation metadata. Candidate sampling is deterministic for a given seed and occurs without replacement; a location can have several verified posed assets.

The publisher's placement_candidates.json must contain the SHA-256 of geometry_file and candidates like:

{
  "geometry_sha256": "SHA256_OF_PEOPLE_FREE_ROOT_LAYER",
  "candidates": [{
    "id": "candidate_01",
    "position": [10,20,0.5],
    "verified_static_collision": true,
    "poses": [{
      "asset_file": "survivor_assets/lying.usda",
      "pose_label": "lying",
      "yaw_degrees": 45,
      "verified_static_collision": true
    }]
  }]
}

Posed assets must have a valid default prim and an origin compatible with the candidate translation. Verification applies to the full posed body at that candidate. The generator trusts publisher verification metadata; it does not run a physics clearance check. Candidate locations must also avoid mutually overlapping bodies when sampled together. The current SHA checks the root geometry layer, so the publisher must freeze referenced dependencies as well.

The generator writes a USD scene that references the selected geometry and adds the sampled survivors, along with ground truth and a task manifest.

Maintainer TODO — complete placement generation

Export scene-specific candidates and posed assets with the dataset bundle. The current generator resamples prepared candidates; it does not yet run the research placement pipeline on arbitrary geometry. Add that pipeline and validate collision clearance if unrestricted new locations or poses are required for release.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Dataset URL is a placeholder: supply the published URL/checksum, or unpack a local bundle. dw run requires the selected scene files to be installed.
  • Out of GPU memory: start with one robot and Frontier/Lawnmower, check other GPU processes, or assign model services to another available GPU. A single GPU must fit the chosen workload; remote deployments are still planned.
  • Existing checkout has changes: setup preserves tracked edits. Use the managed .runtime installation or a separate clean supported checkout; do not point setup at the research fork.
  • Endpoint connection fails: the URL is resolved from containers. Check the server API and reachable host/IP. VLM URLs include /v1.
  • No odometry, takeoff rejected, or clock stalled: inspect container.log and policy logs in the run directory. Failed missions are not scored as completed episodes.
  • Missing USD textures/references: the public bundle must be self-contained. Native USD dependency validation is required before release.
  • PPL unavailable: no validated reference route matches this discovery subset, fleet size and starts. TIP and Progress can still be computed for a completed episode.
  • Already running project: use ./dw down, or a different project name and nonconflicting subnet. Existing research containers are separate from this runtime.

Reach out or raise an issue if you encounter any problems.
